post.description: Dry-run-first repair plans for tombstones and catalogue/metadata path drift (Issue #81).

Atomically rebuild the additive FTS indexes from the current rows.

Recovery tool for a corrupted/divergent derived index: dry-run reports
whether the index counts match the live rows; the real run deletes and
re-creates `__xl_fts`, `__xl_fts_cjk` and `__xl_fts_map` in one table
transaction, so an interrupted rebuild rolls back to the previous index.
Atomically insert a bounded batch of rows keyed by caller-supplied idempotency keys.

get.description: List same-table attachment metadata for currently readable, live source rows. Requires xelibrary:read and table/row ACL. UUID keyset cursor is bound to table and normalized search, not authority; every page checks current identity/ACL. At most 500 references are examined per page; empty pages may have next_cursor. Search is a casefolded substring of filename or displayed source_label. No content, object hash, row values, preview or total count is returned.

Isolated, non-active preview for server-detected PNG attachments.

The object is fully decoded and re-encoded with Pillow, so source chunks
(EXIF/ICC/text) never reach the browser and a corrupt image fails the
request instead of rendering partially. PDF previews need a rendering
dependency decision (issue #152) and stay unsupported here.

get.description: Embedding/index queue view for administrators; reindex itself stays admin-only.
Return only the authenticated caller's XeLibrary indexing jobs.

Per-table index visibility for every reader of the table (issue #72).

Derives live coverage from the table itself instead of the admin-only
job log: rows at their current revision are counted through
__xl_vectors, rows still waiting through __xl_changes.indexed_revision.
Model/chunker staleness is deliberately not folded into these numbers;
search responses already surface it explicitly.
